newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet says Retevision a fundamental move.
newsitem.headline: Stet says Retevision a fundamental move.

text.p: Italian telecoms holding Stet expressed satisfaction on Friday after winning a joint bid for a stake in Spain's Retevision, calling it a fundamental step forward in the company's international growth.
Retevision, Spain's second telephone operator, said earlier on Friday it had awarded the bid for its 60 percent sell-off to a consortium led by Spanish utility Endesa and Stet/Telecom.

"The result represents a fundamental step in the process of internationalisation of the (Stet) which, as was confirmed by our recent global alliance with AT&T, is focused on Europe and Latin America," Tomaso Tommasi di Vignano, Stet managing director, said in a statement.
The winning consortium offered 116.36 billion pesetas ($779.1 million) for 60 percent of Retevision and another 64.64 billion pesetas for an obligatory 10 percent capital expansion.

Stet said it paid some 56.33 billion pesetas as its part of the deal, 36.21 billion of which will go into the actual acquisition with the remaining 20.12 billion being used for the recapitalisation of the Spanish company.
Last week, STET and AT&T Corp of the United States announced they would forge a strategic global telecoms alliance with a focus on Latin America and Europe.
Tommasi said the Spanish market was of primary importance to the overall strategy of the new alliance.

"The entry into Retevision allows us to be present with a key role in Spain, which is Europe's fifth-largest telecoms network and has a turnover of some 20 trillion lire and a strong growth rate," he said.
"The immediate availability, assured by our consortium, of a fibre optics infrastructure will allow us to be operating in very little time," Tommasi said.
"It will also allow us to provide competitive and advanced services, thanks to our know-how and to the advantages of our recent accord with AT&T," he added.
Endesa/Stet plan to start offering a basic Retevision telephone service in one month.

Tommasi also said that a foothold in Spain would help his firm in its drive to expand its business in Latin America, "which because of cultural, linguistic and economic relations is closely tied to the Iberian peninsula".
The choice of the Endesa/STET offer had been widely expected after the group dramatically outbid the other participant Opera, comprised of Spain's BCH , France Telecom and U.S.-based Sprint.
